around.headline: Masked gang attacks four with machetes in Bengaluru's Uttarahalli, police launch manhunt
around.summary: A masked gang wielding machetes attacked four people indiscriminately in southwest Bengaluru's Uttarahalli, leaving them injured, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald. Police have launched a manhunt; avoid the area at night until arrests are made and stay alert if you live nearby.

around.headline: Thieves break into Bengaluru home and steal 500g gold while family was at hospital
around.summary: A family rushed to hospital for a medical emergency returned to find their home broken into and 500 grams of gold stolen, per The Times of India. If you ever have to leave home in a hurry, take a moment to lock up properly and alert a trusted neighbour or your building's security directly rather than announcing it publicly.

around.headline: Heavy vehicles barred during school hours on key Bengaluru stretch as kids face 2-hour daily commutes
around.summary: Police have banned heavy vehicles during school hours on a key stretch after reports that some schoolkids spend nearly two hours on the road each day, per The Times of India and NDTV. Expect diversions on affected routes during morning and afternoon school timings.

around.headline: Pink Line's Bannerghatta metro stretch to open by mid-October after BMRCL gets ISA safety certification
around.summary: BMRCL has received its Independent Safety Assessor certification, clearing the way for the Pink Line's Bannerghatta stretch to open by mid-October, per Deccan Herald. Commuters on that corridor can plan for a metro option within a few weeks.

around.headline: e-Aasthi 2.0: online khata bifurcation for Bengaluru property owners opens September 28
around.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority's e-Aasthi 2.0 platform will let property owners apply for khata bifurcation online from September 28 (with a wider rollout by October 5), per The Hindu, Deccan Herald and The Times of India. Owners should ensure road connectivity records are in order, as that's a stated requirement for approval.
around.source: The Hindu, Deccan Herald, The Times of India

around.headline: IMD issues heavy-to-extremely-heavy rainfall alert for several states over the next 7 days
around.summary: The India Meteorological Department has issued a 7-day forecast warning of heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in several states, and Bengaluru itself is expected to see more rain this week even as the monsoon formally withdraws elsewhere, per ABP Live and The Times of India. Keep an eye on local advisories if you're travelling out of the city this week.
around.source: ABP Live, The Times of India

street_smart.title: You get a call that a family member has been rushed to hospital in an emergency. You need to leave home right now.
street_smart.based_on: Times of India reported today that thieves broke into a Bengaluru home and stole 500 grams of gold while the family was away at the hospital during a medical emergency — a pattern opportunistic thieves specifically watch for.
street_smart.situation: You're panicked and every second feels like it matters. Your keys, phone and wallet are in hand, and you're already halfway out the door.

choices.text: Take 60 seconds to lock all doors and windows properly, and call or message a trusted neighbour or your building's security/watchman directly to keep an eye on the flat, then leave.
choices.feedback: Correct. A minute spent securing the home and alerting someone you actually trust — in person or by direct call, not a public post — closes the exact window opportunistic thieves rely on when a home is left hurriedly unlocked.

choices.text: Grab your things and rush out immediately without stopping to lock up properly, since the emergency is more urgent than the house.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. It feels reasonable in the moment, but an unlocked or poorly secured home during exactly this kind of rushed, distracted exit is what today's Bengaluru burglary case exploited — the family was gone only as long as the hospital visit took.

choices.text: Lock the main door but leave a spare key under the doormat or with a casual acquaintance 'just in case' someone needs to get in.
choices.feedback: Risky. Spare keys in predictable spots (under mats, on ledges) are one of the first things burglars check, and handing a key to someone you don't fully trust creates a new point of failure.

choices.text: Post an update on your neighbourhood WhatsApp or social media group asking people to keep an eye on the house while you're away.
choices.feedback: Risky. A public post — even in a 'local' group — can reach people outside your trusted circle and effectively broadcasts that the house will be empty. A direct call to one or two people you actually trust is safer than a public announcement.

takeaways: Even in a genuine emergency, 60 seconds to lock doors/windows and arm any alarm or CCTV is worth it — thieves target homes left hurriedly unsecured.
Alert a trusted neighbour or your building's security directly (call or in person), not a public WhatsApp/social media group, which can tip off people outside your trusted circle.
Don't keep all valuables like gold in one predictable spot at home — a bank locker or split storage slows down opportunistic thieves even if they get in.

quiz.question: Which Namma Metro line's Bannerghatta stretch is set to open by mid-October, after BMRCL received its safety certification, per Deccan Herald?
quiz.why: The certification comes from an Independent Safety Assessor (ISA), a mandatory sign-off before any new metro stretch can open to the public.

quiz.question: Bengaluru police barred what from a key stretch during school hours this week, after reports that some schoolkids face nearly two-hour daily commutes?
quiz.why: The move targets the specific safety risk of heavy vehicles sharing narrow, congested roads with young children during school timings.

quiz.question: The India Meteorological Department's latest 7-day forecast warns of what for several Indian states, even as Bengaluru itself expects more rain this week?
options: Cyclonic winds only along the coast
quiz.why: The alert comes even as the monsoon formally begins withdrawing from parts of the country — withdrawal doesn't mean rain stops everywhere at once.

quiz.question: In what year was the city officially renamed from Bangalore to Bengaluru?
quiz.why: The renaming took effect on 1 November 2014, part of a wider move to restore Kannada-language names to several Karnataka cities.

quiz.question: Which river is the primary source of drinking water for Bengaluru?
quiz.why: Bengaluru sits outside the Cauvery basin, so the water is pumped uphill over roughly 100 km — one reason the city's water supply is both costly and vulnerable to shortfalls.
